title: Improvement of isometric dorsiflexion protocol for assessment of tibialis anterior muscle strength☆
author: Siddiqi, Arjunan, et al.

steps.title: Position participant and foot plate
steps.instruction: Seat the participant in a sturdy chair, extend the tested leg onto the foot plate so that hip, knee, and ankle are at 90°, 140°, and 90° respectively; place the non‑dominant foot firmly on the ground to prevent instability.

steps.title: Secure ankle and foot with straps
steps.instruction: Fasten a flexible strap around the ankle to the foot plate to prevent heel lift; add a strap at the metatarsal‑phalangeal junction to stop foot movement; add a strap around the toe phalanges to prevent toe‑extension.

steps.title: Prepare skin and place EMG electrodes
steps.instruction: Abrade and clean the skin at each electrode site with an alcohol swab; place Delsys single‑channel active differential silver bar electrodes (10 mm × 1 mm, 10 mm inter‑electrode distance) according to SENIAM positions: TA – 1/3 line between tip of fibula and tip of medial malleolus; SOL – 2/3 line between medial femoral condyle and medial malleolus; MG – most prominent bulge of the muscle belly; LG – 1/3 line between head of fibula and heel.

steps.title: Connect EMG acquisition system
steps.instruction: Link the electrodes to a Myomonitor 4 (Delsys, Boston) system set to gain 1000, CMRR 92 dB, bandwidth 20–450 Hz, roll‑off 12 dB/octave; configure sampling at 1000 Hz with 16‑bit resolution.

steps.title: Attach force sensor to foot plate
steps.instruction: Mount an Interface S‑type force sensor onto the foot plate to record dorsiflexion force.

steps.title: Set foot‑fixing condition
steps.instruction: Choose one of two foot‑fixing settings: (i) existing protocol – foot fixed and ankle immobilized; (ii) same as (i) plus the toe straps described in step 2.

steps.title: Perform maximal voluntary contraction trials
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant to dorsiflex maximally for 5 s; repeat the 5‑s contraction after a 120 s rest; record both attempts and keep the higher value as the MVC. Perform the MVC sequence for each foot‑fixing condition, allowing at least a 5 min rest between the two conditions.

steps.title: Process EMG data and compute RMS
steps.instruction: Discard the first and last 1 s of each 5‑s EMG recording (transients); calculate the root‑mean‑square (RMS) of the remaining 3 s for TA and each triceps‑surae muscle (MG, LG, SOL); sum the three TS RMS values to obtain overall TS RMS.

steps.title: Calculate variability metrics
steps.instruction: Determine the coefficient of variation for the recorded force and for the summed TS EMG RMS across trials.
